critical.issue: Entries diverge across exit methods on identical inputs. On period='2m', asset=BTC/USD, strategies=[hunter,squeeze,continuation]: native=15 entries, atr=12, fixed=7. Root cause: different exit timings change when positions release, shifting the next-entry candidate window (single-position/cooldown gate). Spec explicitly requires identical entries so only exit logic changes — this invariant currently does NOT hold. Fix approach: log ALL entry signals once (exit-agnostic) then simulate each exit against that fixed entry set.

rca of the issue: A/B/C parity fails because the backtest engine advances state (position open/cooldown) using each exit's actual exit-time. When ATR fires earlier than native, the position frees up sooner → more entries later; when Fixed fires much later (1.5d in some cases vs native's 7h), fewer entries fit into the same window. This is why native=15 > atr=12 > fixed=7. To fulfil 'A/B/C testing = same entries, only exit changes', the runner must simulate all three exit modules against the SAME shared entry set (e.g., simulate all entries in parallel per bar, tracking each module's per-entry position independently), OR replay each module against the entries produced by a reference run (e.g., native). The frontend already surfaces the divergence correctly (7/12/15 counts in badges + trade log).
